examples.problem:
Let $V=\mathbb{R}_2[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
\langle {x(t)}, {y(t)} \rangle   = x(0)y(0) + x(1)y(1) + x(-1)y(-1).
$$

Given that $p(t) = 1 + t + t^2$ and $q(t) = kt - t^2$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ in $V,$ find the value of $k.$
examples.worked_solution:
Since $p(t)$ and $q(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1)+p(-1)q(-1) \\  & =(1)(0)+(3)(k-1)+(1)(-k-1) \\  & =0+(3k-3)+(-k-1) \\  & =2k-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $\langle p(t), q(t) \rangle = 0$ and solve for $k\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =0 \\ 2k-4 & =0 \\ 2k & =4 \\ k & =2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.
$$

If $x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and 
$y=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =5\cdot k+3\cdot ((-3)\cdot (-5))+5\cdot 1 \\  & =5k+45+5 \\  & =5k+50\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x,y⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ 5k+50 & =0 \\ 5k & =-50 \\ k & =-10\end{aligned}
$$
